title: Near self-duality and spatial reorganization of anyon vortex lattices
abstract: Contact attraction drives the self-generated vortex lattice of a trapped anyon gas towards self-duality, but integrated energies do not reveal where the remaining departure from it is located. We address this question in the almost-bosonic Chern--Simons--Schrödinger average-field model using a positive, gauge-invariant local defect that measures the covariant kinetic energy in excess of the magnetic bound. Numerically computed low-energy states at three statistical fluxes show that, as the stability line is approached, the integrated defect falls by about two orders of magnitude while the density modulation grows, so that magnetic saturation and density uniformity separate. The residual defect concentrates in a vortex-free outer shell that carries unscreened statistical flux. There it reduces to a smooth radial mismatch between the statistical flow and the density decay, which the interior lattice cannot cancel, whereas the covariant kinetic and amplitude-gradient energies show no comparable enrichment. The effect is robust to grid and box refinement, while its magnitude depends on flux and on the low-energy branch. Exact dilation and contact-response identities relate the squared energy to the density shape and provide consistency checks. Repulsion produces the opposite trend: a smoother density with a larger defect.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes vortex lattices in a trapped anyon gas model to pinpoint where the system deviates from a state of self-duality. By using a specialized local defect measure, the authors show that the residual non-self-dual energy concentrates in a vortex-free outer shell. This reveals a crucial spatial mechanism governing the energy balance in these exotic quantum fluids.
main_problem: The study investigates the spatial distribution of the departure from self-duality in a trapped anyon vortex lattice as attractive interactions are increased.
main_result: The residual defect concentrates in a vortex-free outer shell, resolving a spatial imbalance in the cancellation that produces near self-duality, which is not captured by integrated energy measures alone.
method: The authors use numerical computation of low-energy states and employ a positive, gauge-invariant local defect to measure the excess covariant kinetic energy.
model_or_system: The system is an effective model of a trapped anyon gas described by the almost-bosonic Chern–Simons–Schrödinger (CSS) average-field model. The energy functional involves kinetic, interaction, and potential energy terms.
key_observables: Self-duality Defect ($\delta$), density modulation, covariant kinetic energy, and the local defect ($\delta$).
important_parameters: Statistical flux ($ eta$), attractive interaction strength ($G$), and the stability line ($G_c = -4\pi eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses an effective functional and is not a proof of a simultaneous many-body limit; results are robust to grid refinement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the vortex-free edge at high flux, comparing the azimuthal flow ($ ar{r}v_{	heta}$) and density decay rate ($- ar{r}\partial_r \log  ar{s}$) to demonstrate local self-duality.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the energy functional and key diagnostics (defect $\delta$, scale-invariant quantities $b_{sh}, \eta$), analyzes the effect of attractive interactions approaching the stability boundary, and finally pinpoints the spatial location of the residual defect in the outer shell.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed spatial diagnostics for topological order in synthetic quantum systems, offering insights into how local structure dictates global energy properties in strongly interacting quantum fluids.
